source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper uses the same discrete observational binary-treatment/binary-outcome setup with fixed positivity and proves a scalar regression-mean minimax MSE lower bound (d/(n log n))^2 + 1/n; it does not state a CATE-law W1 theorem.

The paper studies iid draws of parameter pairs from a mixing distribution, observed as two Binomial(t,·) measurements with common fixed t, and proves lower and matching sparse-regime W1 change-law results.
The paper gives local moment matching and positive reconstruction for the sorted discrete probability vector under Wasserstein-equivalent sorted l1 loss, with its stated sparse and dense components.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 2.1, Theorem 1 and Corollary 1; Section 3 and Corollary 2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies smooth mixing densities under observed heterogeneous binomial trial counts and gives pointwise KDE bias/variance and density-difference results; it does not cover unrestricted atomic laws with endogenous unknown target masses.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: State and prove a conditioning-versus-unconditioning comparison lemma that isolates the extra random-occupancy and target-weight terms absent from VinayakKongKakade2019Change; use it as the formal non-subsumption bridge for both the upper and lower routes.

Before committing to a candidate rho(n,d), derive an explicit two-cluster unequal-mass, boundary-overlap bound for the grouped estimator with its factorial covariance displayed; this turns the handle into a discriminating sparse-regime test.
Add a short corollary identifying which branch of L_n is active in each d-versus-n regime, so the proposed frontier has visibly testable transition requirements rather than only a global bracket.
